title: Monthly exchange rates against the US dollar (yen, mark, Swiss franc, sterling) and consumer prices of the United States, Japan, Germany, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, December 1959 - December 1985 (Chapter 46: floating rates and their volatility)
source: Bank for International Settlements, BIS Data Portal: bilateral exchange rates (WS_XRU, monthly averages of observations through the period) and long series of consumer prices (WS_LONG_CPI, index 2010 = 100), CSV answers of the SDMX API (stats.bis.org)
series: month (YYYY-MM); jpy: yen per US dollar; deu_eur: Germany in euro per US dollar, the BIS's conversion of the Deutsche Mark at the fixed rate (the mark = deu_eur x 1.95583); chf: Swiss francs per US dollar; gbp: pounds sterling per US dollar; cpi_us, cpi_jp, cpi_de, cpi_ch, cpi_gb: consumer price indices, 2010 = 100. The values are copied as the API prints them.
license: Source: BIS (Bank for International Settlements), BIS Data Portal. The Data Portal's terms (https://data.bis.org/help/legal): 'The use of the statistics is unrestricted, provided that: if the statistics are reproduced, the BIS must be cited in your publication or product as the source of the statistics; if the statistics will be translated into another language, a statement must be included in your publication or product that the translation is not an official BIS translation' (row bisdata_terms) The labels of the chapter's figures are the book's Chinese, not an official BIS translation.
notes: Chapter 46 uses the series in its text (the yen in July 1971, January and March 1973, October 1978, October 1982 and February 1985; the Swiss franc in October 1978; sterling in February 1985), in Figure floating_rates (1965-1985, index of the 1970 average = 100) and in Figure floating_volatility and the text's standard deviations: the monthly changes of the logarithms of the nominal rate, of the real rate (the nominal rate times the American CPI over the home CPI, eq:external-real) and of the ratio of the two price levels, times 100, January 1960 - December 1970 (132 changes) and January 1974 - December 1985 (144 changes), standard deviations with ddof = 1. The consumer prices of the 1960s often stay unchanged for some months (the British index in 76 of the 132 changes of 1960-1970). The rows bisdata_* of floating_facts quote the lines of the months the text names.
